subject: Forensic retention exception request — Finova Health incident
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finovahealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: request to preserve logs and packet capture from Nov 1 incident

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the quick response during our morning incident call. We have an active regulator inquiry (State Data Authority) and need to preserve a broader set of artifacts than your standard 30-day retention window. Specifically we request: full session logs for tenant finova-prod for the 72-hour window around the incident, audit trail export (admin actions), and the raw network packet capture that we were able to pull locally.

Can Redwood place those artifacts on legal hold for 60 days while we complete regulatory review? We will need a signed chain-of-custody when you hand over the packet captures and a clear deletion timestamp after the hold expires.

I attached an initial evidence_manifest.csv listing candidate files. Please let me know the next steps and any paperwork you need from us.

— Marta
Marta Lopez
Head of SecOps, Finova Health
marta.lopez@finovahealth.com
[attachment: evidence_manifest.csv (csv, 3KB)]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finovahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: request to preserve logs and packet capture from Nov 1 incident

Marta —

Thanks for the note and the manifest. Short answers up front:
- Redwood's default hosted retention for request/session logs is 30 days; we do offer evidence holds for incidents.
- We can place an evidence hold scoped to specific artifacts (by object keys and time range) and export packet captures, but exception approval is required for any hold beyond 30 days.
- We will require a signed retention-exception form and a chain-of-custody acknowledgement before we hand over raw PCAPs.

Please confirm the exact keys / start-end timestamps you want held (you included the manifest which helps). Also confirm whether Finova wants the preserved data stored in our US region S3 bucket or transferred directly to your approved S3 endpoint. If you prefer transfer, we will need an S3 pre-signed path or an SFTP endpoint and a point of contact for transfers.

I will start an internal review to scope operational impact. In the meantime I am cc'ing Karthik (security) and Laura (legal) to speed approvals.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the final artifact list/timestamps.
2) Finova signs the exception + COC form (I can send DocuSign).
3) We initiate preservation and provide an evidence download bundle + signed manifest.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Customer Success (Security Escalations), Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
[internal note: evidence_manifest.csv attached to original request]

Stephanie —

Thanks. Confirming scope:
- Tenant: finova-prod
- Time range: 2027-10-31T22:00:00Z through 2027-11-02T10:00:00Z (UTC)
- Artifacts: session logs (request/response bodies excluded unless necessary), admin audit trail, and the attached sample packet capture we collected.

Attached: network_packet_sample.pcap.gz (sample).

— Marta

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Finova retention exception request — please advise (INC-789)

Folks — forwarding Finova's signed scope and ask (attached manifest + sample). Need quick sign-off on three items so we can respond to regulator timeline:
A) Security approval to export packet captures and to do a one-time S3 transfer to their bucket (they provided contact Jordan Blake).
B) Legal approval for a 60-day retention exception and the DocuSign wording (Laura).
C) Ops: estimate of storage/transfer time and expected deletion timestamp (Vivek).

Suggested guardrails: limit preservation to the exact object keys for the window above; encrypt artifacts with customer KMS (we can use our SSE-KMS and share envelope), attach a signed chain-of-custody that documents MD5/SHA256 of the bundles, and set an automated deletion schedule that triggers on the exception expiry.

Karthik — do you see any technical or compliance blockers here?

— Stephanie

On Tue, 02 Nov 2027 at 08:25 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Stephanie —
>
> Technical OK from security side with the following conditions:

> - All exported bundles must be hashed and the hashes included in the chain-of-custody form.
> - Transfer must be over an enrolled endpoint; S3 with a pre-provisioned IAM role or a short-lived pre-signed PUT window is preferred.
>

>

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@finovahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Forensic retention exception request — Finova Health incident

Marta —

Thank you for the details and patience. Legal and security have reviewed and we can accommodate a 60-day retention hold limited to the items you listed. Summary of the approved plan: 

- Scope: tenant finova-prod; time window 2027-10-31T22:00:00Z through 2027-11-02T10:00:00Z. Artifacts: session logs (excluding plaintext request bodies unless Finova explicitly authorizes), admin audit trail, packet captures supplied by Finova and the export bundle we will produce.
- Hold window: preservation start 2027-11-01T09:00:00-07:00; automatic deletion scheduled on 2028-01-01T09:00:00-07:00 (60 days).
- Transfer method: Redwood will upload a single encrypted bundle to your S3 path (s3://finova-incident-uploads/incoming/redwood/INC-789/) via a short-lived pre-signed PUT you will provide. Contact for transfer and verification: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@finovahealth.com>.
- Custody and verification: Attached chain_of_custody_form.pdf must be signed by Finova POC prior to transfer. Redwood will include MD5 and SHA256 hashes of each file and a signed manifest.
- Legal paperwork: Please sign the retention exception DocuSign packet here: https://docusign.example.com/signer/abc123. We will not commence transfer until DocuSign is completed.
- Cost: Finova will be invoiced for any incremental storage/egress beyond standard support allowances; I can send an estimate if you prefer.

Attachments included here: chain_of_custody_form.pdf (fill & sign), forensic_retention_exception_docusign.pdf (DocuSign packet preview).

Operational notes for Finova: once you accept the pre-signed PUT we will begin the export within 24 business hours and email an evidence bundle link and checksum file. After your confirmation of the checksum we will mark custody as transferred in our records. The automatic deletion will still be triggered by the exception expiry unless you request an extension via the same process and obtain approvals.

If that aligns with your regulator's needs please complete DocuSign and return the signed chain-of-custody. We will then schedule the transfer.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Customer Success (Security Escalations), Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
[attachments: chain_of_custody_form.pdf, forensic_retention_exception_docusign.pdf]
